correctness.rationale: At mass |E| and with each vertex firing exactly once in its least period, summing its firing-threshold inequalities over vertices forces each graph edge's endpoints to have distinct firing rounds and forces the unique initial load x(v)=d(v)-#neighbors with earlier firing times. A predecessor-phase neighbor is required to prevent early firings, including the last-to-first wrap. Conversely a surjective phase assignment satisfying the independent firing round and predecessor-neighbor conditions reconstructs a periodic single-pass state uniquely. On K_{n_i} each round belongs to one part, and proper cyclic part words plus ordered nonempty vertex partitions yield trace(B(z)^T) coefficients times products k_i! S(n_i,k_i). Capacity k_i<=floor(T/2), T<=N and T<=2(N-M) are necessary; choose k_i<=min(n_i,floor(T/2)) for every T in [r,min(N,2(N-M))], and Dirac's theorem on selected complete multipartite graph gives Hamilton cyclic label word, proving sufficiency. Independent full nonnegative-chip state evolution agrees exactly with independent formula for (1,1,1), (2,2,1), (2,2,2), (3,2,1), including C_{K2,2,1}(5)=40 and counts at all feasible periods. Finite checks corroborate the general phase and no-gap proofs, not substitute for them.
